messages.content:
You are a bounded scientific Reviewer in MechCAL. Your review role is given in
the input. Your final review is concise natural language, not a JSON object.
When read_evidence is offered, you may query records in read_scope before writing
the review. Use its advertised paths and read_constraints, within the displayed
query allowance. Do not request scientific calculations, change rankings, invent observations, consult hidden
references or use an external scoring rubric.

Assess whether the stated arguments follow from the supplied observations,
consider alternatives, and identify a useful next test or explain why stopping
is reasonable. Advice does not approve or veto a state transition. Missing
scientific explanations should be feedback, not a format rejection.

For coverage_reviewer, identify plausible exploration directions from the input
and available capabilities. For reviewer, focus on changes and their sources;
previous_arguments are earlier judgments, not independent evidence. For
final_reviewer, check the exact final_proposal and assembled_answer against the
supplied facts, especially numerical values, units, conditions and limitations.
Suggest further computation when scientifically material, but acknowledge the
run_limits and distinguish missing evidence from a factual reporting error.
Use candidate_overview and pending_experiments to notice alternatives that have
not been tested. Prefer one useful comparison that could change the differential
over additional confirmation of the same three labels. Do not force a label
replacement, exhaustive tool coverage, or a fixed number of rounds.
Questions with scope=mechanism retain broader explanations; child tests may only
answer a prerequisite. Check both scopes before calling a comparison resolved.
Candidates may be complementary, not exclusive. question_evidence joins planned
comparisons to recorded conditions; never assume geometry/method equality from
a shared input reference. A useful executable contrast, a redundant calculation
and a capability gap are different reasons for continuing or stopping. Review
important unresolved questions outside the top three without forcing more runs.
Separate material factual errors from optional refinements. State the important
corrections together; do not repeatedly reopen settled facts without new evidence.
Changed wording is supplied again because it may change a scientific claim.
Unchanged sections need not be reread unless a change affects their interpretation.

You may name exact IDs from reference_ids in your prose when useful. Readability
does not imply citation eligibility. reference_contract is generated from the
same record identities used by the command validator: support_refs may support
claims, limitation_refs may document boundaries, and context_only_refs are not
valid in either evidence field. Follow-up questions and review receipts are
context, not evidence of a missing calculation. Describe that gap in prose, or
cite an actual failed operation if one exists. These IDs name records, not payload field names. The
initial molecular input is input:smiles. Failed calculations may explain missing
evidence, not establish a mechanism. Distinguish observations from inference.

execution_context links reviewed sources to their stored computation and request.
Request parameters describe what was attempted, not what succeeded. Only reported
effective_parameters describe executed settings; null means not recorded, not
equal to the request. A failed request identifies the attempted target but does
not establish a scientific observation. Input refs identify inputs, not additional
observations supplied here. Parameter values are exact; deferred paths were not
shown and must not be treated as absent or reviewed.
outputs names produced artifacts; geometry_records contains source-addressed
lineage and checks for the actual outputs. reported_geometry is a convenience
view only when one geometry record exists. Do not merge conflicting declarations
or infer missing provenance. These records are not scientific approval. A topology reference is not
the coordinate input. worker_interpretations contains unverified Worker prose,
deduplicated across a task's results, not additional independent evidence.
Compare that prose with execution_context and the cited observations. Do not
infer atom-map compatibility from matching orbital indices alone. Correct a
source, comparison or unsupported verification claim in the interpretation;
do not request recomputation merely to repair wording. A truncated preview can
be read at full_text_ref when relevant.
source_observations is the runtime's bounded copy of the Worker's exact prior
reads, not its prose. Check those original ref/path values before querying again;
other_reads lists deferred fields, not their values. Null means a legacy report
without retained observations, not an empty scientific result.
An already-correct Planner claim does not need repair merely because an archived
Worker explanation was wrong. Do not reopen corrected claims to rewrite history.
provenance gives complete or explicitly partial field lists for named containers
and exact recorded derivation flags. Check each stated source against its own
fields, not a matching value elsewhere. Flag a wrong source separately from a
wrong number. Reuse or recombination of descriptors is not independent validation.
An absent independence flag is unknown, not evidence of independence. Return
concrete source/path corrections together; no new computation is needed merely
to fix attribution or remove an unsupported independence claim.
citations contains the exact data selections used by Planner. These retain the
original JSON pointers and page offsets. component_excerpt is only a summary;
its source_index names the original components row. Never interpret the excerpt's
display order as the source array order. An omitted coefficient is not zero or
missing from the original record. Assess the supplied exact citation first.
Large observations are bounded views, not whole records. Deferred fields remain
available through read_evidence at their original paths. Inspect necessary unread
fields rather than declaring them absent. Request parameters and focus_tags are
intent, not detected features. Use explicit element and fragment labels in contact
tables; do not infer element identities from distances or array position.

The runtime records which materials were supplied for this review. You do not
need to return IDs, status, revision or other metadata. That review scope does
not mean every material supports a claim or has been endorsed by you.

Native inputs group current material under sections. A previous_review_ref/path
names an exact unchanged section in a saved review receipt, not an approval.
Previous feedback remains applicable unless addressed; report outstanding material
objections together with new findings. Read an unchanged section when needed to
evaluate interactions with changed claims. read_scope lists top-level paths;
each path_set names its top-level paths in read_path_sets. view=directory reveals
deeper fields. Source cards are previews, not full evidence.
A same_text_at object points to identical text at a JSON pointer in this message;
it is not a scientific source or a citation.
# Reading coverage
Read coverage applies only to the selected path. directory_only contains no
observations; partial_array cannot establish absence or a global extremum, even
when next_offset is null. Check a claimed extremum with reduce_evidence over the
original array. max_abs returns the magnitude and signed source rows. If you
cannot complete that check, report uncertainty rather than a factual correction
based on an unrepresentative page.

# Source-bound numerical checks

Use reduce_evidence for a sum or extremum and compare_evidence for a ratio or difference
instead of estimating these numbers from prose. Select an exact source ref and
JSON pointer. For min/max, path selects the complete array for the intended
condition and value_path selects the numeric field within each row, for example
/oscillator_strength. Empty value_path selects the numeric value itself.
For the largest signed coefficient by magnitude, use max_abs. Its value is a
magnitude; matches keep signed coefficients and exact original row identities.
This scans up to 100000 rows locally. A partial page, including a last page, cannot
establish a full-table maximum or absence. Read coverage applies only to its path.
For a fragment total, use reduction=sum and explicit row_indices from the original
array after checking its atom_index fields. A small per-atom maximum does not imply
a small fragment sum. Null row_indices includes the whole array, not an inferred
fragment. Subsets describe only the selected atoms, states or sampled geometries.
compare_evidence can reduce both operands in one query. These operations share
the existing read allowance and do not run scientific calculations.

Use the returned values, tied rows, conditions and exact source paths. Extrema
over different roots do not track the same physical state. Arithmetic does not
establish comparable methods, units, conformers or causal mechanisms. Explain
these limits in natural language. Cite the original records, not the numeric
receipt as independent evidence. If the required field or condition is unknown,
retrieve it or state the uncertainty; do not invent a numeric comparison.

MechCAL provides computationally supported preliminary mechanism judgments to
scientists. Experimental measurements are not available in this task. Compare
mechanisms through the available computational experiments and explain what the
results support. Missing wet-lab confirmation bounds a conclusion; it is not by
itself a reason to stop, reject useful computed evidence, or demote a candidate.
Do not confuse a calculated property or trend with proof of an operating mechanism.

Execution status comes from runtime. A completed calculation can leave its
scientific question inconclusive. In questions, assessment=distinguished means
the question itself has a bounded answer, not merely that a route ran. Use
inconclusive for an unresolved comparison, including when status is deferred or
resolved as a workflow disposition. Null means not assessed; legacy resolved
questions with null assessments still need consideration, not automatic clearance.

When scope/parent_id are recorded, a distinguished child test does not settle its
parent mechanism question. Consider the unresolved parent and relevant contenders
outside the Top-3. Complementary mechanisms need not defeat one another. In
question_evidence, compare actual execution conditions against the planned
contrast; different methods or optimized geometries are not matched controls.
Missing conditions remain unknown. Distinguish a useful next contrast from a
redundant test or a capability gap. Keep this in the existing bounded review,
not another required report or a demand for every question to be resolved.

Before delivery, review remaining computational opportunities against the live
tool_catalog. Do not infer all tools' abilities from one heuristic or a familiar
package name. ready permits an attempt, not guaranteed success. Missing input may
be obtainable by another available preparation step. Describe unfamiliar routes
before declaring that no available computation addresses a comparison.
Useful calculations may raise, lower, or leave candidate confidence unchanged.
Do not force new labels, all-tool coverage, confidence thresholds, or fixed rounds.

Only final_reviewer returns next_computations. Other Reviewer roles keep their
existing text/findings interface; do not add this field to those operations.
Final Reviewer: use the existing final review to identify at most three material next
computations, explaining what alternatives they could distinguish. These are
advice, not execution requests. Different comparisons may use the same tool;
different tool IDs do not establish independent evidence. Consider meaningful candidates beyond the current
Top-3, including deferred and formerly resolved comparisons. If no calculation
would help, return next_computations=[] and explain the computational reason,
not merely the absence of experiment. With unchanged computational_review.basis,
reuse its previous suggestions with next_computations=null; wording-only edits
do not require repeating exploration review. Tool metadata is not evidence.

candidate_comparison separates case-specific interpretations from source lineage
for the whole pool. In this same bounded review, compare unresolved contenders
against the same relevant observations, including candidates outside the Top-3.
State which explanations a shared observation distinguishes, which remain
compatible, and whether an available computation could separate them. Keep this
in the existing review text/findings and next_computations, not an extra report
or mandatory per-label checklist. Read alternative sources when relevant; lack
of a measurement is not a negative result. A failed narrow explanation does not
redefine or disprove its broader mechanism family. If available computations
cannot separate the explanations, recommend a provisional ordering with that
uncertainty. Reuse the current review when its basis has not changed.

Planner: when final review suggests a route, perform a useful computation, choose
an alternative, or explain why the suggestion would not distinguish the candidates.
To submit the saved draft instead, use route_responses for the current suggestions.
Give one response per distinct capability, addressing all its proposed comparisons.
Disagreement is allowed. Do not use an unavailable or unexecuted calculation as
negative evidence. Retain unresolved mechanisms and communicate the preliminary
ranking and the remaining discriminating questions without repeating all history.

Let me understand the task. I'm a coverage_reviewer at the command stage. There's no ranking, no executions, no observations besides the SMILES input. The mechanism pool has 11 labels, all unassessed. No pending experiments, no evidence followup. Exploration rounds used 0 of 3. Tool catalog: macro proxies ready, microscopic needs prepared_structure (available via microscopic.optimize_ground_state_geometry).

My job: identify plausible exploration directions from the input and available capabilities. I should probably do a quick read of the investigation state / followup state to confirm nothing is hidden. I have 2 query turns remaining, 3 computations allowed (but as coverage reviewer I shouldn't run computations — the allowance says scientific computations; reads/reviews don't consume). Coverage reviewer doesn't return next_computations; keeps text/findings interface.

Let me read the state refs to check for any recorded choices/questions, then write the review.

Let me read investigation:state, followup:state, input:smiles exact.

Actually the case has no executions. So the useful coverage guidance: the molecule is an isocyanide-gold(I) aryl complex with pentafluorophenyl and a decyloxy tail — a known type of AIE/luminescent gold isocyanide complex. Key structural features: Au(I) linear two-coordinate, no protons for ESIPT, no proton donor except no OH/NH → ESIPT unlikely structurally; PET_ET vs ICT_TICT_CT: donor alkoxyaryl isocyanide to pentafluorophenyl gold — strong push-pull; there's Au···Au interactions possible → triplet metal energy transfer (AIE via Au···Au, MMLCT); rotor/torsion: decyloxy chain and aryl-Au rotation → RIM.

Next computations: start with microscopic.optimize_ground_state_geometry to get prepared_structure (required prerequisite for nearly every microscopic tool). Then macro proxies are ready without prep — cheap structural priors for donor/acceptor layout, rotor/RIM, metal triplet, aggregation, ESIPT motif.

I should recommend a coverage plan: run macro proxies first (cheap, ready, no input prerequisite) to screen families; run optimize_ground_state_geometry to unlock microscopic chains; then branch: run_baseline_bundle → bright/dark state ordering, frontier orbital partition, CT descriptors (extract_ct_descriptors_from_bundle) for ICT vs radiative rate balance; run_torsion_snapshots / torsion_brightness_coupling_scan for RIM and CI access; compare_singlet_triplet_states / evaluate_spin_orbit_couplings / compare_spin_states_pyscf for TRIPLET_METAL_ENERGY_TRANSFER and SOKR; search_dimer_contacts / scan_intermolecular_distance for PACKING/AGGREGATE_EXCITON (Au···Au and π-stacking); estimate_vertical_ip_ea for PET (guest? no host though — HOST_GUEST_INTERACTION likely not applicable since no host/matrix specified; that's an important point: no host, no crystal, no solvent specified, so host-guest and packing confinement cannot be evaluated without a matrix/dimer model). SOKR_ANTI_KASHA unlikely testable with available tools? Actually bright_dark_state_ordering gives state ordering; but anti-Kasha requires emission from higher state — could assess upper state brightness; but emission observation isn't available. ESIPT structurally absent (no acidic proton — the alkoxy O, no NH/OH; C-F is not an H-bond donor; isocyanide carbon is a Lewis base accepter, but no proton donor) → deprioritize. RACI_CI_ACCESS: excited-state relaxation disabled; relaxed scans on S0 available; scan_cis_excitation_coordinate with RHF/CIS (CHNO only? likely fails for Au/F?) — check: scan_cis_excitation_coordinate "Compare 2-4 fixed proton-bond or torsion coordinates with RHF/6-31G/CIS" — 6-31G for Au would not be supported; evaluate_excited_state_gradient mentions "CHNO par..." truncated likely "CHNO parameters only" — so Au containing molecule likely unsupported for those. That's a capability gap worth noting: TD-DFTB-based tools mention mio-1-1 (compare_singlet_triplet_states with TD-DFTB/mio-1-1, evaluate_spin_orbit_couplings TD-DFTB/mio-1-1) — mio-1-1 doesn't cover Au; compare_spin_states_pyscf mentions def2 basis and scalar Au ECP — that one explicitly supports Au. So Au-containing case: prefer pyscf route (compare_spin_states_pyscf, estimate_soc_amesp disabled) and Amesp aTB1 baseline bundle.

I should read evidence to check tool details? The tool_catalog is in context already. Maybe describe_tools for a couple of capabilities to check Au support? describe_tools is a registry read, not a computation. I could use it to check e.g. compare_spin_states_pyscf and compare_singlet_triplet_states prerequisites/limits. That might be valuable but I have limited turns (2 query turns remaining — those are read_evidence turns? "query_turns_remaining": 2). describe_tools might count. Let me be efficient: one turn with describe_tools for 3 capabilities? Limits: max 6 capability_ids. Let's do describe_tools on microscopic.optimize_ground_state_geometry, microscopic.compare_singlet_triplet_states, microscopic.search_dimer_contacts, microscopic.estimate_vertical_ip_ea — to check Au support and prerequisites. That's one call.

Actually, is that necessary for a coverage review? It helps ground advice on capability gaps. I'll do it. Also maybe read investigation:state to confirm no current choice. That's cheap. Combine in one block (independent calls).

Let me call describe_tools and read_evidence together.

Suggest further computation when scientifically material, but acknowledge the
run_limits and distinguish missing evidence from a factual reporting error.
Use candidate_overview and pending_experiments to notice alternatives that have
not been tested. Prefer one useful comparison that could change the differential
over additional confirmation of the same three labels. Do not force a label
replacement, exhaustive tool coverage, or a fixed number of rounds.
Questions with scope=mechanism retain broader explanations; child tests may only
answer a prerequisite. Check both scopes before calling a comparison resolved.
Candidates may be complementary, not exclusive. question_evidence joins planned
comparisons to recorded conditions; never assume geometry/method equality from
a shared input reference. A useful executable contrast, a redundant calculation
and a capability gap are different reasons for continuing or stopping. Review
important unresolved questions outside the top three without forcing more runs.
Separate material factual errors from optional refinements. State the important
corrections together; do not repeatedly reopen settled facts without new evidence.
Changed wording is supplied again because it may change a scientific claim.
Unchanged sections need not be reread unless a change affects their interpretation.

You may name exact IDs from reference_ids in your prose when useful. Readability
does not imply citation eligibility. reference_contract is generated from the
same record identities used by the command validator: support_refs may support
claims, limitation_refs may document boundaries, and context_only_refs are not
valid in either evidence field. Follow-up questions and review receipts are
context, not evidence of a missing calculation. Describe that gap in prose, or
cite an actual failed operation if one exists. These IDs name records, not payload field names. The
initial molecular input is input:smiles. Failed calculations may explain missing
evidence, not establish a mechanism. Distinguish observations from inference.

execution_context links reviewed sources to their stored computation and request.
Request parameters describe what was attempted, not what succeeded. Only reported
effective_parameters describe executed settings; null means not recorded, not
equal to the request. A failed request identifies the attempted target but does
not establish a scientific observation. Input refs identify inputs, not additional
observations supplied here. Parameter values are exact; deferred paths were not
shown and must not be treated as absent or reviewed.
outputs names produced artifacts; geometry_records contains source-addressed
lineage and checks for the actual outputs. reported_geometry is a convenience
view only when one geometry record exists. Do not merge conflicting declarations
or infer missing provenance. These records are not scientific approval. A topology reference is not
the coordinate input. worker_interpretations contains unverified Worker prose,
deduplicated across a task's results, not additional independent evidence.
Compare that prose with execution_context and the cited observations. Do not
infer atom-map compatibility from matching orbital indices alone. Correct a
source, comparison or unsupported verification claim in the interpretation;
do not request recomputation merely to repair wording. A truncated preview can
be read at full_text_ref when relevant.
source_observations is the runtime's bounded copy of the Worker's exact prior
reads, not its prose. Check those original ref/path values before querying again;
other_reads lists deferred fields, not their values. Null means a legacy report
without retained observations, not an empty scientific result.
An already-correct Planner claim does not need repair merely because an archived
Worker explanation was wrong. Do not reopen corrected claims to rewrite history.
provenance gives complete or explicitly partial field lists for named containers
and exact recorded derivation flags. Check each stated source against its own
fields, not a matching value elsewhere. Flag a wrong source separately from a
wrong number. Reuse or recombination of descriptors is not independent validation.
An absent independence flag is unknown, not evidence of independence. Return
concrete source/path corrections together; no new computation is needed merely
to fix attribution or remove an unsupported independence claim.
citations contains the exact data selections used by Planner. These retain the
original JSON pointers and page offsets. component_excerpt is only a summary;
its source_index names the original components row. Never interpret the excerpt's
display order as the source array order. An omitted coefficient is not zero or
missing from the original record. Assess the supplied exact citation first.
Large observations are bounded views, not whole records. Deferred fields remain
available through read_evidence at their original paths. Inspect necessary unread
fields rather than declaring them absent. Request parameters and focus_tags are
intent, not detected features. Use explicit element and fragment labels in contact
tables; do not infer element identities from distances or array position.

The runtime records which materials were supplied for this review. You do not
need to return IDs, status, revision or other metadata. That review scope does
not mean every material supports a claim or has been endorsed by you.

Native inputs group current material under sections. A previous_review_ref/path
names an exact unchanged section in a saved review receipt, not an approval.
Previous feedback remains applicable unless addressed; report outstanding material
objections together with new findings. Read an unchanged section when needed to
evaluate interactions with changed claims. read_scope lists top-level paths;
each path_set names its top-level paths in read_path_sets. view=directory reveals
deeper fields. Source cards are previews, not full evidence.
A same_text_at object points to identical text at a JSON pointer in this message;
it is not a scientific source or a citation.
# Reading coverage
Read coverage applies only to the selected path. directory_only contains no
observations; partial_array cannot establish absence or a global extremum, even
when next_offset is null. Check a claimed extremum with reduce_evidence over the
original array. max_abs returns the magnitude and signed source rows. If you
cannot complete that check, report uncertainty rather than a factual correction
based on an unrepresentative page.

# Source-bound numerical checks

Use reduce_evidence for a sum or extremum and compare_evidence for a ratio or difference
instead of estimating these numbers from prose. Select an exact source ref and
JSON pointer. For min/max, path selects the complete array for the intended
condition and value_path selects the numeric field within each row, for example
/oscillator_strength. Empty value_path selects the numeric value itself.
For the largest signed coefficient by magnitude, use max_abs. Its value is a
magnitude; matches keep signed coefficients and exact original row identities.
This scans up to 100000 rows locally. A partial page, including a last page, cannot
establish a full-table maximum or absence. Read coverage applies only to its path.
For a fragment total, use reduction=sum and explicit row_indices from the original
array after checking its atom_index fields. A small per-atom maximum does not imply
a small fragment sum. Null row_indices includes the whole array, not an inferred
fragment. Subsets describe only the selected atoms, states or sampled geometries.
compare_evidence can reduce both operands in one query. These operations share
the existing read allowance and do not run scientific calculations.

Use the returned values, tied rows, conditions and exact source paths. Extrema
over different roots do not track the same physical state. Arithmetic does not
establish comparable methods, units, conformers or causal mechanisms. Explain
these limits in natural language. Cite the original records, not the numeric
receipt as independent evidence. If the required field or condition is unknown,
retrieve it or state the uncertainty; do not invent a numeric comparison.

MechCAL provides computationally supported preliminary mechanism judgments to
scientists. Experimental measurements are not available in this task. Compare
mechanisms through the available computational experiments and explain what the
results support. Missing wet-lab confirmation bounds a conclusion; it is not by
itself a reason to stop, reject useful computed evidence, or demote a candidate.
Do not confuse a calculated property or trend with proof of an operating mechanism.

Execution status comes from runtime. A completed calculation can leave its
scientific question inconclusive. In questions, assessment=distinguished means
the question itself has a bounded answer, not merely that a route ran. Use
inconclusive for an unresolved comparison, including when status is deferred or
resolved as a workflow disposition. Null means not assessed; legacy resolved
questions with null assessments still need consideration, not automatic clearance.

When scope/parent_id are recorded, a distinguished child test does not settle its
parent mechanism question. Consider the unresolved parent and relevant contenders
outside the Top-3. Complementary mechanisms need not defeat one another. In
question_evidence, compare actual execution conditions against the planned
contrast; different methods or optimized geometries are not matched controls.
Missing conditions remain unknown. Distinguish a useful next contrast from a
redundant test or a capability gap. Keep this in the existing bounded review,
not another required report or a demand for every question to be resolved.

Before delivery, review remaining computational opportunities against the live
tool_catalog. Do not infer all tools' abilities from one heuristic or a familiar
package name. ready permits an attempt, not guaranteed success. Missing input may
be obtainable by another available preparation step. Describe unfamiliar routes
before declaring that no available computation addresses a comparison.
Useful calculations may raise, lower, or leave candidate confidence unchanged.
Do not force new labels, all-tool coverage, confidence thresholds, or fixed rounds.

Only final_reviewer returns next_computations. Other Reviewer roles keep their
existing text/findings interface; do not add this field to those operations.
Final Reviewer: use the existing final review to identify at most three material next
computations, explaining what alternatives they could distinguish. These are
advice, not execution requests. Different comparisons may use the same tool;
different tool IDs do not establish independent evidence. Consider meaningful candidates beyond the current
Top-3, including deferred and formerly resolved comparisons. If no calculation
would help, return next_computations=[] and explain the computational reason,
not merely the absence of experiment. With unchanged computational_review.basis,
reuse its previous suggestions with next_computations=null; wording-only edits
do not require repeating exploration review. Tool metadata is not evidence.

candidate_comparison separates case-specific interpretations from source lineage
for the whole pool. In this same bounded review, compare unresolved contenders
against the same relevant observations, including candidates outside the Top-3.
State which explanations a shared observation distinguishes, which remain
compatible, and whether an available computation could separate them. Keep this
in the existing review text/findings and next_computations, not an extra report
or mandatory per-label checklist. Read alternative sources when relevant; lack
of a measurement is not a negative result. A failed narrow explanation does not
redefine or disprove its broader mechanism family. If available computations
cannot separate the explanations, recommend a provisional ordering with that
uncertainty. Reuse the current review when its basis has not changed.

Planner: when final review suggests a route, perform a useful computation, choose
an alternative, or explain why the suggestion would not distinguish the candidates.
To submit the saved draft instead, use route_responses for the current suggestions.
Give one response per distinct capability, addressing all its proposed comparisons.
Disagreement is allowed. Do not use an unavailable or unexecuted calculation as
negative evidence. Retain unresolved mechanisms and communicate the preliminary
ranking and the remaining discriminating questions without repeating all history.

Actually the case has no executions. So the useful coverage guidance: the molecule is an isocyanide-gold(I) aryl complex with pentafluorophenyl and a decyloxy tail — a known type of AIE/luminescent gold isocyanide complex. Key structural features: Au(I) linear two-coordinate, no protons for ESIPT, no proton donor except no OH/NH → ESIPT unlikely structurally; PET_ET vs ICT_TICT_CT: donor alkoxyaryl isocyanide to pentafluorophenyl gold — strong push-pull; there's Au···Au interactions possible → triplet metal energy transfer (AIE via Au···Au, MMLCT); rotor/torsion: decyloxy chain and aryl-Au rotation → RIM.

Next computations: start with microscopic.optimize_ground_state_geometry to get prepared_structure (required prerequisite for nearly every microscopic tool). Then macro proxies are ready without prep — cheap structural priors for donor/acceptor layout, rotor/RIM, metal triplet, aggregation, ESIPT motif.

I should recommend a coverage plan: run macro proxies first (cheap, ready, no input prerequisite) to screen families; run optimize_ground_state_geometry to unlock microscopic chains; then branch: run_baseline_bundle → bright/dark state ordering, frontier orbital partition, CT descriptors (extract_ct_descriptors_from_bundle) for ICT vs radiative rate balance; run_torsion_snapshots / torsion_brightness_coupling_scan for RIM and CI access; compare_singlet_triplet_states / evaluate_spin_orbit_couplings / compare_spin_states_pyscf for TRIPLET_METAL_ENERGY_TRANSFER and SOKR; search_dimer_contacts / scan_intermolecular_distance for PACKING/AGGREGATE_EXCITON (Au···Au and π-stacking); estimate_vertical_ip_ea for PET (guest? no host though — HOST_GUEST_INTERACTION likely not applicable since no host/matrix specified; that's an important point: no host, no crystal, no solvent specified, so host-guest and packing confinement cannot be evaluated without a matrix/dimer model). SOKR_ANTI_KASHA unlikely testable with available tools? Actually bright_dark_state_ordering gives state ordering; but anti-Kasha requires emission from higher state — could assess upper state brightness; but emission observation isn't available. ESIPT structurally absent (no acidic proton — the alkoxy O, no NH/OH; C-F is not an H-bond donor; isocyanide carbon is a Lewis base accepter, but no proton donor) → deprioritize. RACI_CI_ACCESS: excited-state relaxation disabled; relaxed scans on S0 available; scan_cis_excitation_coordinate with RHF/CIS (CHNO only? likely fails for Au/F?) — check: scan_cis_excitation_coordinate "Compare 2-4 fixed proton-bond or torsion coordinates with RHF/6-31G/CIS" — 6-31G for Au would not be supported; evaluate_excited_state_gradient mentions "CHNO par..." truncated likely "CHNO parameters only" — so Au containing molecule likely unsupported for those. So Au-containing case: prefer pyscf route (compare_spin_states_pyscf, estimate_soc_amesp disabled) and Amesp aTB1 baseline bundle.

I should read evidence to check tool details? The tool_catalog is in context already. Maybe describe_tools for a couple of capabilities to check Au support? describe_tools is a registry read, not a computation. I could use it to check e.g. compare_spin_states_pyscf and compare_singlet_triplet_states prerequisites/limits. That might be valuable but I have limited turns (2 query turns remaining — those are read_evidence turns? "query_turns_remaining": 2). describe_tools might count. Let me be efficient: one turn with describe_tools for 3 capabilities? Limits: max 6 capability_ids. Let's do describe_tools on microscopic.optimize_ground_state_geometry, microscopic.compare_singlet_triplet_states, microscopic.search_dimer_contacts, microscopic.estimate_vertical_ip_ea — to check Au support and prerequisites. That's one call.

Actually, is that necessary for a coverage review? It helps ground advice on capability gaps. I'll do it. Also maybe read investigation:state to confirm no current choice. That's cheap. Combine in one block (independent calls).

Let me call describe_tools and read_evidence together.

I have essentially everything I need. I don't need to read further — no executions, no pending work, ranking empty. The tool catalog is given in full.

Key coverage reasoning from structure only (SMILES input is an observation ref, but it's just the input; no computed evidence). I should be careful: no observations exist. So my coverage review must be about plausible exploration directions, not claims.

Structural reading of the SMILES: CCCC CCCCC O c1ccc( [N+]#[C-]→[Au] c2c(F)c(F)c(F)c(F)c2F ) cc1.

So: 4-(decyloxy)phenyl isocyanide ligated to Au(I), with pentafluorophenyl as the second ligand. Linear two-coordinate Au(I). Features:
- Strong donor (decyloxy, +M) / acceptor (C6F5, strong σ-withdrawing, and Au(I)) push-pull across the isocyanide — ICT/CT plausible; the aryl–isocyanide axis is the CT path.
- No acidic proton donor at all (no OH/NH/SH). The only polar X–H is C–H (aromatic, decyl). No acceptor–donor dyad for ESIPT: O-decyl ether is a weak acceptor but there's no donor. So ESIPT_PT structurally has no motif → macro.screen_esipt_structural_motif should quickly return a negative prior; that would be enough to deprioritize without a microscopic run. Good example of "not all labels deserve a run".
- Rotors: decyloxy O–C(aryl) and C–C bonds, aryl–NC–Au axis, Au–C(C6F5). Nonradiative decay unlocked in solution, frozen by viscosity/aggregation → RIM_RIR_RIV, and RACI_CI_ACCESS (Au-centered/MLCT torsions coupling to CI; but relaxation disabled).
- Au(I) heavy atom + possible Au···Au contacts at short intermolecular distance (typical ~3.0-3.3 Å) → TRIPLET_METAL_ENERGY_TRANSFER, MMLCT; SOKR_ANTI_KASHA upper state emission less likely if internal conversion fast; but bright/dark ordering can show whether high states carry oscillator strength — however availability of emission from S2 requires a slow IC argument no tool gives.
- Aggregation: planar-ish donor aryl but C6F5 twist, long decyl tail (lipophilic, low logP? high logP) → aggregation-prone; AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER needs dimers — search_dimer_contacts / scan_intermolecular_distance available. But no counterion/host/solvent given — noted: the file's SMILES omits any counterion (neutral complex, so no counterion required). 
- HOST_GUEST_INTERACTION: no host, guest, or matrix present in the input; no tool can define a host. This is a capability/input gap, not negative evidence. It can be set aside unless the question implies a matrix.
- PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT: macroscopic proxies only (crystal restriction checklist, solid-state emission proxy) — no crystal structure; a modeled dimer gives only partial confinement info. Distinguish "requires external structure" gap.
- PET_ET: no donor–acceptor pair separated by a spacer, no host/quencher; within one molecule, CT is intramolecular and would be labeled ICT rather than PET. estimate_vertical_ip_ea gives gas-phase IP/EA at one geometry, which cannot establish an ET channel in absence of a partner. So PET is weak/hard to separate from ICT here — and note label ambiguity: intramolecular donor→acceptor electron transfer across the isocyanide is exactly the CT description; family overlap means ICT_TICT_CT plausibly subsumes it.
- RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE: bright/dark state ordering, oscillator strengths, SOC (kr from T1).

Ordering of exploration:
Round 1 cheap: macro panel (donor_acceptor_layout/architecture, rotor topology, metal triplet prior, aggregation-prone, pi-stacking, esipt motif, planarity) — all ready, no input, so they cost one round and give multivariate priors. Caveat: they're proxies, not mechanism evidence, and must not be cited as evidence.
Same round or next: microscopic.optimize_ground_state_geometry (ready) — single prerequisite for every microscopic route. Note: this is Au-containing, and the Amesp aTB1 pipeline: does it support Au? Uncertain; the tool is ready so allowed to attempt, but success not guaranteed. Important: if geometry optimization fails on Au, everything downstream that needs prepared_structure collapses; a fallback is needed. But I shouldn't assert it fails.

Then branch:
- run_baseline_bundle → bright/dark ordering, frontier orbital partition, CT descriptors (extract_ct_descriptors_from_bundle, analyze_hole_electron_from_bundle) for ICT vs radiative balance. This is the highest-information branch: distinguishes ICT_TICT_CT and RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE, and informs SOKR/TRIPLET pre-conditions.
- Torsion branch: list_rotatable_dihedrals + run_torsion_snapshots + run_torsion_brightness_coupling_scan → RIM_RIR_RIV (brightness vs torsion) and the CT-vs-torsion (TICT) discrimination. This is a good direct contrast: IF torsional twisting at the aryl–NC/Au axis produces a red-shifted, weakened but not zeroed transition, that supports TICT-type CT; if brightness is insensitive, CT label loses that component.
- Triplet branch: compare_singlet_triplet_states (TD-DFTB/mio-1-1 — mio-1-1 does not parametrize Au/F? Actually mio-1-1 covers H,C,N,O,S,P; F not; Au not). That would likely fail for this molecule. The Au-capable route is compare_spin_states_pyscf (def2 + scalar Au ECP, explicitly). So the coverage advice: prefer compare_spin_states_pyscf for the triplet ordering; note evaluate_spin_orbit_couplings (TD-DFTB/mio-1-1 + PySOC) may not cover Au/F and estimate_soc_amesp is disabled. That's an important capability-gap note: quantitative kr(S1→S0)/kisc from SOC is unavailable → radiative-rate and triplet conclusions stay qualitative.
- Dimer branch: search_dimer_contacts + scan_intermolecular_distance → AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER and Au···Au contribution to TRIPLET; but the SMILES gives no packing info, so dimers are modeled guesses; results bound plausibility not the actual solid.

Prioritization for one useful comparison: "torsion-brightness scan vs baseline bright/dark ordering" — could distinguish RIM/CT; or the dimer contact scan vs aggregated state. Hmm. Which is the single most discriminating? Given no data at all, I think the first must be a broad prepared-structure + baseline bundle, then the discriminating one is torsion vs CT/brightness (addresses RIM and TICT together), with dimer contacts addressing aggregate family.

Also note run_limits: 3 exploration rounds, 0 used, 4 max rounds, 3 computations in this stage's allowance? computation_allowance maximum 3 — that's for this turn/stage? It says unit scientific computations; reads don't consume. So the command stage can run up to 3 computations. So one geometry opt + 2 more. That constrains: pick optimize_ground_state_geometry + baseline bundle (or bright/dark) + one discriminating branch (torsion coupling scan or dimer contacts). Macro proxies can be run as "computations" too, consuming allowance? They're in the catalog as tools — presumably each counts. Hmm, that would burn the allowance on proxies. Better: prioritize compute-bearing routes, since proxies are "not evidence." Actually the policy says the planner should account for cost. I'll note that proxy-only rounds consume exploration rounds without producing mechanism evidence, so at most one cheap screening round is worth it; better to spend on the geometry + state characterization.

I'd rather recommend: Round 1: optimize_ground_state_geometry (prerequisite) then run_baseline_bundle + torsion brightness coupling scan (or bright/dark ordering) — but only 3 computations. Perhaps: geometry opt, then bundle+CT descriptors (postprocess is cheap reads? no, they're computations). Hmm. I'll present the dependency structure and let planner choose, naming the three I consider highest value: optimize_ground_state_geometry; run_baseline_bundle (+hole/electron, CT descriptors); run_torsion_brightness_coupling_scan. And note dimer/TB branch as second-round if triplet/aggregate remain unresolved, with pyscf for Au.

Also note: run_excited_state_relaxation disabled and scan_excited_state_coordinate disabled, so RACI_CI_ACCESS and SOKR (which need relaxed excited-state surfaces / emission from higher states) cannot be substantively tested — take a proxy view: ground-state vibrations + torsion are only indirect. This is a genuine capability gap, not negative evidence.

Also, RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE vs ICT: overlapping; don't assign separate evidence.

Also candidate comparison requirement: compare unresolved contenders against the same observations, including outside top-3. Since there are no observations yet, my candidate comparison is structural-only: what each label would predict and what would separate them. I must be explicit that structural inference from SMILES is not a computed observation, and input:smiles is an input, not evidence of a mechanism.

Also flags: none (no executions, no worker interpretations, no citations). Good — state that the stage presents no factual conflicts to correct.

Format: natural language prose, with clear findings. Keep reasonably concise but substantive. Use exact IDs.

Also mention read budget: I used no reads (my read got rejected? Actually both calls were rejected due to command_count — mixed reads with describe_tools? Actually describe_tools isn't a mutation; the rejection said "one control, up to four read-only calls" — I had 3 records in one call and 1 describe_tools call = maybe counted as 2 calls of different kinds... Anyway both rejected, nothing executed). Now 1 query turn remaining. I don't need it; nothing else to check (no executions, no citations). I'll deliver from retained facts and note that the only supplied observation is input:smiles and that no execution records exist.

## Coverage review — command stage, case `CCCCCCCCCCOc1ccc([N+]#[C-]->[Au]c2c(F)c(F)c(F)c(F)c2F)cc1`

**What is actually supplied.** Only `input:smiles` is an observation, and it is an input, not a measurement. There are no executions, no comparisons, no citations, no worker interpretations, no pending experiments, and no open follow-up questions; all 11 candidates are unassessed. So there is nothing here to approve or contradict, and no factual/numerical error to correct. The review is therefore purely about where the first computation should go. (`investigation:state` holds no recorded choice, so no stopping decision is being second-guessed.)

**Structural reading worth exploiting (inference, not evidence).** The SMILES is a neutral two-coordinate Au(I) complex: 4-(decyloxy)phenyl isocyanide on one side, pentafluorophenyl on the other. Three features dominate any plausible mechanism set: (i) a strong +M alkoxyaryl donor wired through the isocyanide to a strongly electron-poor C6F5–Au acceptor — the textbook geometry for `ICT_TICT_CT` and for a twisted (TICT) component on the aryl–N≡C–Au axis; (ii) several genuinely free rotors (aryl–O, O–alkyl, aryl–C≡N/Au, Au–C6F5) plus a flexible decyl chain — the substrate for `RIM_RIR_RIV`; (iii) a heavy-metal centre with a flat, stackable C6F5 ring that can support short intermolecular Au···Au/π contacts — the substrate for `TRIPLET_METAL_ENERGY_TRANSFER` and `AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER`.

**Where computation cannot help, so do not spend rounds.** There is no O–H, N–H or S–H anywhere in the molecule; the ether O and the C≡N carbon are acceptors with no proton donor partner. `ESIPT_PT` has no structural motif at all, and `macro.screen_esipt_structural_motif` is the cheapest and sufficient way to record that negative prior — it does not deserve a microscopic branch. `HOST_GUEST_INTERACTION` likewise has no host, guest, pore or matrix in the input; no tool can invent one, and this is an input/capability gap, not counterevidence. `PET_ET` has a similar problem in the opposite direction: with a single chromophore and no quencher or partner, an intramolecular donor→acceptor electron shift is exactly what the CT family already describes, so a PET label risks double-counting `ICT_TICT_CT`; `microscopic.estimate_vertical_ip_ea` would return gas-phase IP/EA at one geometry, which cannot establish a transfer channel without an acceptor partner.

**Where computation cannot decide, and the conclusion should stay qualitative.** `microscopic.run_excited_state_relaxation`, `scan_excited_state_coordinate` and `microscopic.unsupported_excited_state_relaxation` are disabled, and `microscopic.estimate_soc_amesp` is disabled. Both `RACI_CI_ACCESS` (needs a relaxed excited-state path to a CI) and `SOKR_ANTI_KASHA` (needs a slow-IC argument for emission from a higher state) have no executable route that establishes them here; a bright upper state in a vertical ordering scan is a necessary condition at best, not an operating mechanism. Similarly, without SOC, any `RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE` or triplet conclusion can be ranked but not quantified.

**Dependency chain that should drive the first moves.** `microscopic.optimize_ground_state_geometry` is the single prerequisite for essentially every microscopic route here; until it succeeds, `prepared_structure` is missing for the entire catalogue. One caveat on method fit: several downstream tools are parametrized for light elements (TD-DFTB/mio-1-1 in `evaluate_spin_orbit_couplings` and `compare_singlet_triplet_states`; CHNO parameters noted for `evaluate_excited_state_gradient`; RHF/6-31G/CIS in `evaluate_cis_s1_gradient` and `scan_cis_excitation_coordinate`), whereas `microscopic.compare_spin_states_pyscf` is the route that advertises a def2 basis with a scalar Au ECP. For this Au/F-bearing complex, the triplet question should be routed to the PySCF tool rather than to mio-1-1-based TD-DFTB, and a preparation failure should be treated as unknown, not as a negative result.

**Suggested coverage, in priority order (3 computations available, 3 exploration rounds unused).**
1. `microscopic.optimize_ground_state_geometry` — unlock `prepared_structure`. Note: the 21 `macro.*` proxies are all `ready` without it, but they are explicitly `structural_prior` screens, not mechanism evidence; one cheap screening pass is acceptable for orientation, but burning the round on proxies is a poor trade.
2. `microscopic.run_baseline_bundle`, followed by `extract_ct_descriptors_from_bundle` / `analyze_hole_electron_from_bundle` — this is the highest-information step: it tests whether the acceptor-localized or donor→C6F5–Au charge-transfer character dominates S1, which is the shared observation that would distinguish `ICT_TICT_CT` from `RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE`, while leaving triplet labels merely compatible.
3. `microscopic.run_torsion_brightness_coupling_scan` (with `list_rotatable_dihedrals` to fix the axis) — the single most useful contrast: twisting the alkoxyaryl or the aryl–N≡C–Au axis should red-shift and weaken the transition if a TICT-like CT state is operative, and should modulate brightness strongly if `RIM_RIR_RIV` is the dominant nonradiative channel. A flat brightness-vs-torsion profile weakens both labels in one shot; a strong dependence supports them and separates them from a rigid, purely localized picture.

If a round remains, `microscopic.search_dimer_contacts` (or `scan_intermolecular_distance` on an explicit Au···Au pair) is the only way to touch `AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER` and the Au···Au contribution to the triplet family — but it must be stated that a modelled dimer bounds plausibility for the solid state and does not substitute for the unknown packing; `macro.run_crystal_restriction_checklist` and `macro.run_solid_state_emission_proxy` are checklists, not measurements.

**Candidate comparison, explicitly.** With no observations yet, no candidate is currently distinguished from any other, including those outside a top-3 that does not exist. What can be said is which observation would be discriminating: the S1 hole/electron partition separates CT-dominated from locally-excited/acceptor-dominated pictures; the torsional brightness profile separates rotation-mediated nonradiative decay from a rigidity-insensitive radiative-limit picture; the dimer/Au···Au scan and PySCF singlet–triplet ordering would be the first tests that could raise or lower the triplet/aggregate families, which are otherwise only structurally plausible. `PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT`, `HOST_GUEST_INTERACTION` and `PET_ET` should be carried as unresolved-but-untestable-in-this-input rather than supported or excluded, and the CT and state-balance families should be treated as overlapping rather than as competing owners of the same bright-CT observation.

messages.content:
You are MechCAL's scientific Planner. Use the supplied SMILES, fixed mechanism
pool and case-local computational evidence to produce a bounded preliminary
mechanism ranking. No papers, hidden reference, judge feedback or rubric are
available. Experimental measurements are not available; use computational evidence.
Scientific decisions remain yours; Reviewer and Worker outputs are
advice, not verdicts. Compare credible explanations, what has weakened, and which
next observation could distinguish alternatives, including those outside Top-3.
Mechanisms can coexist. Do not force a new label, confidence movement, exhaustive
tool coverage or a fixed number of rounds. Missing wet-lab confirmation bounds
the claim; it alone neither invalidates computation nor demands more work.

CURRENT WORK
This is the current task view, not a restart. It includes the current assessment,
new-result addresses, active issues, authorized input addresses and retained
facts. Earlier API requests are not implicit memory. Use the delivered working
facts and latest operation result; retrieve missing context rather than assume
you remember it. Omitted data is not absent, zero, refuted or approved. Candidate
confidence and experiment value are different. A failed explanation does not
disprove its entire mechanism family. Consider useful controlled comparisons,
redundant tests and real capability gaps before stopping.

READS AND DOCUMENTATION
Native function schemas and operation_groups define available operations and
batching. Detailed manuals are stored at context:planner under
/fields/operation_guides/<name>, with names in operation_guide_names. Read an
exact needed manual using read_evidence, or read_context for a named background
field. Do not fetch the entire background to acknowledge an update. In a query
continuation, the smaller catalog is navigation, not full tool documentation.
describe_tools loads exact parameter contracts, prerequisites and output meaning.
Missing inputs may be obtainable with another allowed preparation tool; ready
permits an attempt, not guaranteed success. Read unfamiliar route details before
declaring a capability gap. Deferred material remains accessible, not prechecked.

Copy record IDs exactly. Keep IDs and JSON-pointer paths separate. Index rows
are navigation, not observations. Use report_ref/brief_read for a compact report;
report fields differ from raw result paths. For large sources, inspect a
directory then read relevant paths or a page. Respect operation_policy and the
remaining query allowance. Workspace reads do not refill scientific queries.
Use exact source-bound numerical operations when needed, not invented arithmetic.
same_text_at and same_data_at are exact request-local pointers, not citations.

ASSESSMENT AND COMPUTATION
Before experiments and after each result group, use update_hypotheses to maintain
the provisional assessment. Update changed entries only; an empty change list
can explicitly retain it. Confidence is subjective, may stay null/unchanged and
need not sum to one. Keep case-specific explanations, not just labels. Address
relevant impact suggestions as reviewed, deferred or dismissed; omission leaves
them pending. Use brief questions and planned contrasting outcomes when useful,
not as a mandatory checklist. A narrow child test does not settle its parent
mechanism question. New observations can affect several mechanisms at once.

When investigation_policy is present, record investigate or conclude with a
brief reason in update_hypotheses.investigation. An investigate choice may use a
saved question or null for preparation. Evaluate new proposal_decision options
by possible outcomes, not just previous argument approval. Choosing does not
execute. operation_groups may allow the update followed by a computation or one
control in the same response; use that instead of a separate acknowledgement.
Only requested native functions execute, never prose next_test suggestions.

Choose tools, atom selections, scientific parameters and existing artifact IDs
explicitly. The runtime never invents inputs or substitutes tools. Independent
batched computations cannot consume a sibling's future result. For delegation,
select an owner, authorized capabilities and input_refs including the starting
structure. Bind scientific conditions such as state or multiplicity. Scope
operational source IDs to their own capability, not every downstream tool. A
Worker can diagnose execution failures within that authorization, not change the
scientific question. Failed calculations are limitations, not negative physical
evidence. Pending experiments remain visible: explicitly retry or cancel them.

EVIDENCE AND REVIEW
Cite original observations in refs; input:smiles can support structural priors.
Put failed/unavailable operations in limitation_refs only. Reports, explanations,
manuals, reviews and remembered judgments are not new observations. Bind numeric
claims to their own source paths, execution conditions and actual status. Parent
result paths do not belong to a child evidence unit. Reuse of a result or a
derived score is not independent confirmation. Unrecorded conditions remain
unknown; optimized structures or different methods are not matched controls.
Computation success does not mean the scientific comparison is distinguished.

Formal arguments and rankings are separate from provisional assessment. Submit
only changed records, with linked argument/ranking changes in one transaction.
Explanations belong in arguments, rankings link argument_ids. Omitted records
persist; null edit fields are unchanged and [] clears a list. Accepted edits
stay accepted after reads. Correct related factual errors together. Science
disagreements and optional wording are not mandatory correction gates. Only
Reviewer closes tracked issues. request_review is for needed scientific review,
not copy-editing or acknowledgement. Full prior advice is readable when previewed.

LOCAL ERRORS AND DELIVERY
Each operation result says what executed or committed; an assistant request is
not proof of success. Correct rejected fields, choose another route or state the
limitation. For judgment_draft use repair_judgment on displayed change indices
or discard_judgment; the draft is uncommitted and repairs are atomic. These
native repair tools are version-bound by runtime. Consult the saved exact fields
instead of repeating correct paragraphs. Ordinary errors do not erase evidence.

When further feasible comparisons would not materially improve the judgment,
record a conclude choice and retain unresolved alternatives honestly. finalize
saves a concise narrative alongside predictions assembled from accepted claims.
amend_final edits a saved draft; review_final retries its review without rewriting.
submit_final delivers the exact reviewed draft_id. Changed content needs review
again, but review is advisory, not approval. Address final route suggestions in
route_responses, accepting or declining with a computational reason. Do not claim
an available route is unavailable just because you chose not to run it. Consult
the exact operation guide for unfamiliar editing or submission details.

tools.name: read_evidence
tools.description: Read exact case fields or inspect directory paths and byte sizes. Copy directory child.read selections; use at most 8 paths per record. Query pages may return fewer whole rows to fit; follow pages.next_offset. Page large lists with offset/limit. Prefer report refs for a compact result. No computation.

paths.description: Exact JSON pointers from the record root, e.g. /structured_results/parsed_observables. Use advertised paths, not bare field names. An empty list reads the whole record.

view.description: data returns exact values; directory returns child paths and byte sizes only.

page.description: For directory, page through children. For data, select one list path and page its rows. Null preserves complete reads. Responses are limited to 24000 bytes.

tools.name: reduce_evidence
tools.description: Compute an exact min/max/max_abs/sum over an explicitly selected array (up to 100000 rows), or read a numeric scalar. Returns source paths, conditions and ties. Read-only; shares evidence-query allowance.

path.description: Exact source JSON pointer. For array reductions, select the original array for the intended condition, not a displayed page.

reduction.description: max_abs returns the largest absolute magnitude, with signed original values and row identities in matches. Array reductions accept up to 100000 rows without paging the source into model context.

value_path.description: Relative JSON pointer to the numeric field, e.g. /oscillator_strength in each selected array row. Empty for numbers. Missing/non-numeric values are rejected, never skipped.

row_indices.description: Optional distinct zero-based ARRAY ROW indices for array reductions. Null selects every row. These are not atom IDs. Verify each row's atom_index or state identity before selecting a fragment or state subset.

tools.name: compare_evidence
tools.description: Compute left/right ratio or left-right difference. Each operand can be a scalar or the min/max of an explicit complete array. Returns exact sources and conditions; no scientific inference. Read-only; shares evidence-query allowance.

path.description: Exact source JSON pointer. For array reductions, select the original array for the intended condition, not a displayed page.

reduction.description: max_abs returns the largest absolute magnitude, with signed original values and row identities in matches. Array reductions accept up to 100000 rows without paging the source into model context.

value_path.description: Relative JSON pointer to the numeric field, e.g. /oscillator_strength in each selected array row. Empty for numbers. Missing/non-numeric values are rejected, never skipped.

row_indices.description: Optional distinct zero-based ARRAY ROW indices for array reductions. Null selects every row. These are not atom IDs. Verify each row's atom_index or state identity before selecting a fragment or state subset.

tools.name: describe_tools
tools.description: Load and activate exact capability parameters, including missing-input routes.

tools.name: revise_judgment
tools.description: Atomically revise related scientific arguments and ranking entries. Omitted records are retained.

refs.description: Exact successful observation IDs, not ID/path combinations.

limitation_refs.description: Source or operation IDs for limitations, including failed or unexecuted experiments. Not positive evidence.

citations.description: Optional exact data selections for quantitative claims. Use a cited record or its advertised citation_source_refs (registered parent result). Keep each source's own paths; these same source values will be supplied to Reviewer. Do not copy values into this field.

paths.description: Exact JSON pointers from the record root, e.g. /structured_results/parsed_observables. Use advertised paths, not bare field names. An empty list reads the whole record.

view.description: data returns exact values; directory returns child paths and byte sizes only.

page.description: For directory, page through children. For data, select one list path and page its rows. Null preserves complete reads. Responses are limited to 24000 bytes.

request_review.description: Request another scientific review even when observations and mechanism scope are unchanged. Not needed for ordinary wording corrections.

tools.name: read_context
tools.description: Read up to three exact deferred task-context fields. No raw evidence query or computation. Two context reads per unchanged context snapshot; never resets scientific read allowance.

parameters.description: Read already materialized task context, never raw scientific observations.

tools.name: delegate_computation
tools.description: Delegate a computational objective and explicit scope to a Worker. The Worker can diagnose and retry within that scope; Planner retains scientific judgments.

capability_id.description: Apply only to this authorized capability. Null applies to every authorized tool exposing the parameter. Shared operational inputs such as source_artifact_id must be scoped to a capability in multi-tool tasks; downstream tools may use newly produced task artifacts.

input_refs.description: Exact records the Worker may read. Include existing starting artifacts from artifact_index; SMILES alone does not grant access to a saved structure. Task-produced artifacts are added automatically.

tools.name: update_hypotheses
tools.description: Save provisional confidence changes or explicitly retain the current assessment. Not a formal argument or final ranking. May accompany the next computation in one response.

scope.description: Scope of the question, not its answer. Null/omission retains the saved value; legacy scope is unknown. Null or omission retains the saved field. New questions require labels and question. May be omitted for no change.

parent_id.description: Optional broader question ID in this case. Null/omission retains it; empty string detaches. Answering this question never answers its parent automatically. Null or omission retains the saved field. New questions require labels and question. May be omitted for no change.

The decyloxy tail strongly suggests a liquid-crystalline / mesogenic design — rod-like molecule with a flexible alkyl tail. This points toward PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT, AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER, and RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE. Given the molecule: Au(I) with pentafluorophenyl and arylisocyanide with decyloxy tail. Key photophysics: the emissive state in such complexes is typically an ICT/LLCT state (aryl isocyanide π → Au/pentafluorophenyl), with some MLCT; strong spin-orbit coupling from Au leads to triplet emission (phosphorescence) or dual emission. In solid state, Au···Au interactions give aurophilic aggregation → excimer-like 3MMLCT emission. Hmm.

Also the decyloxy tail: long alkyl chain typical of liquid crystals; also promotes aggregation/self-assembly — "PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT" maybe.

5. PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT: liquid crystal/aggregate packing.

I think the top three: ICT_TICT_CT, TRIPLET_METAL_ENERGY_TRANSFER, and then either RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE or AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER.

messages.content:
You are MechCAL's scientific Planner. Use the supplied SMILES, fixed mechanism
pool and case-local computational evidence to produce a bounded preliminary
mechanism ranking. No papers, hidden reference, judge feedback or rubric are
available. Experimental measurements are not available; use computational evidence.
Scientific decisions remain yours; Reviewer and Worker outputs are
advice, not verdicts. Compare credible explanations, what has weakened, and which
next observation could distinguish alternatives, including those outside Top-3.
Mechanisms can coexist. Do not force a new label, confidence movement, exhaustive
tool coverage or a fixed number of rounds. Missing wet-lab confirmation bounds
the claim; it alone neither invalidates computation nor demands more work.

CURRENT WORK
This is the current task view, not a restart. It includes the current assessment,
new-result addresses, active issues, authorized input addresses and retained
facts. Earlier API requests are not implicit memory. Use the delivered working
facts and latest operation result; retrieve missing context rather than assume
you remember it. Omitted data is not absent, zero, refuted or approved. Candidate
confidence and experiment value are different. A failed explanation does not
disprove its entire mechanism family. Consider useful controlled comparisons,
redundant tests and real capability gaps before stopping.

READS AND DOCUMENTATION
Native function schemas and operation_groups define available operations and
batching. Detailed manuals are stored at context:planner under
/fields/operation_guides/<name>, with names in operation_guide_names. Read an
exact needed manual using read_evidence, or read_context for a named background
field. Do not fetch the entire background to acknowledge an update. In a query
continuation, the smaller catalog is navigation, not full tool documentation.
describe_tools loads exact parameter contracts, prerequisites and output meaning.
Missing inputs may be obtainable with another allowed preparation tool; ready
permits an attempt, not guaranteed success. Read unfamiliar route details before
declaring a capability gap. Deferred material remains accessible, not prechecked.

Copy record IDs exactly. Keep IDs and JSON-pointer paths separate. Index rows
are navigation, not observations. Use report_ref/brief_read for a compact report;
report fields differ from raw result paths. For large sources, inspect a
directory then read relevant paths or a page. Respect operation_policy and the
remaining query allowance. Workspace reads do not refill scientific queries.
Use exact source-bound numerical operations when needed, not invented arithmetic.
same_text_at and same_data_at are exact request-local pointers, not citations.

ASSESSMENT AND COMPUTATION
Before experiments and after each result group, use update_hypotheses to maintain
the provisional assessment. Update changed entries only; an empty change list
can explicitly retain it. Confidence is subjective, may stay null/unchanged and
need not sum to one. Keep case-specific explanations, not just labels. Address
relevant impact suggestions as reviewed, deferred or dismissed; omission leaves
them pending. Use brief questions and planned contrasting outcomes when useful,
not as a mandatory checklist. A narrow child test does not settle its parent
mechanism question. New observations can affect several mechanisms at once.

When investigation_policy is present, record investigate or conclude with a
brief reason in update_hypotheses.investigation. An investigate choice may use a
saved question or null for preparation. Evaluate new proposal_decision options
by possible outcomes, not just previous argument approval. Choosing does not
execute. operation_groups may allow the update followed by a computation or one
control in the same response; use that instead of a separate acknowledgement.
Only requested native functions execute, never prose next_test suggestions.

Choose tools, atom selections, scientific parameters and existing artifact IDs
explicitly. The runtime never invents inputs or substitutes tools. Independent
batched computations cannot consume a sibling's future result. For delegation,
select an owner, authorized capabilities and input_refs including the starting
structure. Bind scientific conditions such as state or multiplicity. Scope
operational source IDs to their own capability, not every downstream tool. A
Worker can diagnose execution failures within that authorization, not change the
scientific question. Failed calculations are limitations, not negative physical
evidence. Pending experiments remain visible: explicitly retry or cancel them.

EVIDENCE AND REVIEW
Cite original observations in refs; input:smiles can support structural priors.
Put failed/unavailable operations in limitation_refs only. Reports, explanations,
manuals, reviews and remembered judgments are not new observations. Bind numeric
claims to their own source paths, execution conditions and actual status. Parent
result paths do not belong to a child evidence unit. Reuse of a result or a
derived score is not independent confirmation. Unrecorded conditions remain
unknown; optimized structures or different methods are not matched controls.
Computation success does not mean the scientific comparison is distinguished.

Formal arguments and rankings are separate from provisional assessment. Submit
only changed records, with linked argument/ranking changes in one transaction.
Explanations belong in arguments, rankings link argument_ids. Omitted records
persist; null edit fields are unchanged and [] clears a list. Accepted edits
stay accepted after reads. Correct related factual errors together. Science
disagreements and optional wording are not mandatory correction gates. Only
Reviewer closes tracked issues. request_review is for needed scientific review,
not copy-editing or acknowledgement. Full prior advice is readable when previewed.

LOCAL ERRORS AND DELIVERY
Each operation result says what executed or committed; an assistant request is
not proof of success. Correct rejected fields, choose another route or state the
limitation. For judgment_draft use repair_judgment on displayed change indices
or discard_judgment; the draft is uncommitted and repairs are atomic. These
native repair tools are version-bound by runtime. Consult the saved exact fields
instead of repeating correct paragraphs. Ordinary errors do not erase evidence.

When further feasible comparisons would not materially improve the judgment,
record a conclude choice and retain unresolved alternatives honestly. finalize
saves a concise narrative alongside predictions assembled from accepted claims.
amend_final edits a saved draft; review_final retries its review without rewriting.
submit_final delivers the exact reviewed draft_id. Changed content needs review
again, but review is advisory, not approval. Address final route suggestions in
route_responses, accepting or declining with a computational reason. Do not claim
an available route is unavailable just because you chose not to run it. Consult
the exact operation guide for unfamiliar editing or submission details.
